{{nihongo|'''{{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-kami|ja|五十猛神|simple|User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-kami|en:draft|fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-kami1=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}}'''|五十猛神|}}, also read as Itakeru-no-mikoto,<ref name="itakiso-jinja.net" /> is a [[kami]] and the son of [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]] and the god of forests and forestry he is worshipped in {{ill|Itakiso shrine|en|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Itakiso shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itakiso shrine|qq=}}<ref name="my secret Wakayama-2016">{{Cite web|date=2016-10-09|title=Itakiso-jinja Shrine|url=https://www.mysecretwakayama.com/introduce/388/|access-date=2024-03-20|website=my secret Wakayama|language=en}}</ref><ref name="itakiso-jinja.net">{{Cite web|title=Itakiso-Jinja Shrine|url=https://itakiso-jinja.net/m/about_en.html|access-date=2024-03-20|website=itakiso-jinja.net}}</ref> and at {{ill|Takase Shrine|en|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Takase Shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takase Shrine|qq=}}<ref name=". A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史">{{Cite web|title=Isotakeru • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史|url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/isotakeru/|access-date=2023-10-20|website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="shintoshrines">{{Cite web|title=Japan Shinto Kami Gods {{!}} Iso Takeru 五十猛神 {{!}} Rods Shinto|url=https://www.rodsshinto.com/iso-takeru|access-date=2023-10-20|website=shintoshrines|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Aragona|first=Jared|title=from Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697, Vol. 1|url=https://open.maricopa.edu/worldmythologyvolume1godsandcreation/chapter/from-nihongi-chronicles-of-japan-from-the-earliest-times-to-a-d-697-vol-1/|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Magatsubi no Kami and Motoori Norinaga's Theology|url=https://www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp/ijcc/wp/cpjr/kami/ueda.html|access-date=2023-10-20|website=www2.kokugakuin.ac.jp}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023">{{Cite web|date=2023-05-25|title=Isotakeru {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230525152851/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9391|access-date=2024-03-24|website=web.archive.org}}</ref>

He is only called Isotakeru in the [[Nihon Shoki]]. He is called {{ill|Oyabiko|ja|大屋毘古神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oyabiko|qq=}} in the [[Kojiki]].<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" /><ref name="itakiso-jinja.net" />

According to the [[Nihon_Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]] and his son Isotakeru had been driven out of the land of [[Takamagahara|Takamagahara]] and had landed in {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla|1=Silla}}.<ref name="Yoshiki" /> However, they did not like that land and said it was inhospitable so they travelled by boat to [[Izumo_Province|Izumo]].<ref name="itakiso-jinja.net" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023" /><ref name="Yoshiki" /> There, Susanoo handed over the seeds of the tree he had brought from Takamagahara to Isotakeru and ordered him to sow the seeds all over Japan. <ref name="Yoshiki" />

Isotakeru, along with his younger sisters {{ill|Oyatsuhime and Tsumatsuhime|ja|オオヤツヒメ・ツマツヒメ}}, began to sow seeds all over Japan, turning the entire country into forests, finally arriving in the "country of trees", or {{ill|Kii Province|en|Kii Province|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province|1=Kii Province}}..<ref name="Yoshiki">{{cite book|title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido|last1=Yoshiki|first1=Emi|date=2007|publisher=PHP Institute|isbn=978-4569669304|language=Japanese}}</ref>

A different version of the legend suggests that Susanoo, envious of the prosperity of the land of Han, extracted numerous hairs from his body, which he transformed into a vast assortment of trees. This act was intended to bestow the wealth of timber upon the people. Following this event, his three offspring, Isotakeru, Oyatsuhime, and Tsumatsuhime, took it upon themselves to scatter the seeds of these trees throughout Japan. Subsequently, they settled in the region of Kii. <ref name=". A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史" /> Different hairs from different parts of his body produced different species.<ref name="shintoshrines" />

Much later in the Kojiki during the story of the {{ill|Hare of Inaba|en|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Hare of Inaba|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hare of Inaba|qq=}} he protected [[Ōkuninushi|Onamuchi]] when he was being pursued by his eighty brothers.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023" /><ref>{{cite book|title=Kojiki|last1=Philippi|first1=Donald L.|date=2015|publisher=Princeton University Press|pages=96–97}}</ref><ref>Chamberlain (1882). [http://sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj029.htm SECT. XXII.—Mount Tema.]</ref>

{{ill|Itakiso shrine|en|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Itakiso shrine|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itakiso shrine|qq=}} was originally located on what is the site of [[Hinokuma_Shrine|Hinokuma Shrine]] but during the reign of {{ill|Emperor_Suinin|en|Emperor_Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin|1=Emperor Suinin}} was relocated to a place called "Anomori" near its current location, and then relocated again to its present site in 713. <ref name="Yoshiki" />
